name: Devenzi Map Studio – OpenStreetMap, 3D Maps, Store Locator & Routes
author: devenzi

sections.description:
Embedding Google Maps usually means an iframe you cannot style, no places of your own, an API key with a credit card and, on top of that, a cookie banner. Map Studio works differently. It gives you modern vector maps based on OpenStreetMap, and you design them in a full-screen editor made for maps instead of filling in forms.

Use it as a store locator for your branches, a Google Maps alternative for your contact page, a location map with your own pins and markers, or an interactive map with areas and routes.

Highlights

  • A store locator with search, categories, “Near me” and opening hours.
  • 3D buildings that rise when you tilt the map, all the way to the horizon.
  • Light and sky: day, morning, evening, night, or live with the sun as it stands right now at your place.
  • Routes along real roads and paths by car, bike or on foot, with stops you drag and no key needed.
  • Your brand colour for the whole map, pins, areas and buttons.
  • A full-screen studio: click a place on the map and change it right there.
  • No API key, no account, and if the map loads only after a click, no cookie banner either.

Store locator without Google

Start with the “Store finder” template, or add a list to any map:

  • Bring in your locations for free from Excel or CSV, or from WP Store Locator, WP Go Maps or WP Maps.
  • Visitors search your list, filter by category or open now, and call a location with one tap.
  • “Near me” sorts by distance from the visitor’s location, or from a postcode or town they type (with suggestions from your locations), and they can limit the radius from 5 to 100 km.
  • “Do we deliver to you?”: visitors check an address against the areas you drew.
  • “Get directions” in the popup, a direct link to each location, and group bubbles when you have many.
  • GDPR-friendly: nothing from Google on your page, no API key, optional “load after click”.

Designing, not filling in forms

  • The map fills the screen, and three steps lead you from the design to your website.
  • Menus instead of long settings pages: every choice is shown as it will look.
  • Search an address or business with suggestions, or click a station, shop or café on the map and add it as a place.
  • Undo and redo, keyboard shortcuts, and a preview as visitors see it on computer, tablet and phone.
  • Start empty or with a template: store finder, delivery area, hiking route, event site plan.
  • Import places and shapes from a table (CSV/Excel; addresses are found automatically), Google My Maps (KML) or GeoJSON.

Your brand colour

Six map styles: light, night, colourful, clear, fjord and “Brand colour”, which recolours the whole map, pins, areas and buttons from one colour.

Your own places

  • 66 icons or a photo, as drop, circle, square or just the icon, in any size and colour, for the whole map or per place.
  • Popups with formatted text, photos to swipe through, a button to your page and “Get directions”. They open on click, on hover or stay open, beside the map or on it.
  • Stations, shops and cafés of the map, and your places on them, show their photo, opening hours and lines from OpenStreetMap; Getting there lists the stops nearby with minutes on foot.
  • A 360° photo at the top of the popup and a Street View button (Mapillary, or Google with your own key).
  • Opening hours with “Open · until 18:00” right in the popup and the list.
  • Categories as tags; highlight important places with a bigger pin, and keep them out of group bubbles.

Areas and routes

  • Draw a delivery zone, a district or a walking route on the map, or let Map Studio draw delivery areas from real travel times.
  • Plan a route along real roads, pick one of several ways, and it keeps its turn-by-turn directions.
  • Areas show their size and can have their name in the middle; routes show their length, start and finish.

3D and more

3D buildings far into the distance, a compass to turn the map, fullscreen and “my location” buttons, a night style for visitors in dark mode, and the map can be kept to one area. The map library loads only when a map comes into view.

Privacy-friendly (GDPR)

  • Optionally the map loads only after a click (“load after click”), with your own notice text.
  • A privacy page in the admin shows what is loaded when, plus a ready-made text for your privacy policy.

Saved maps and shortcode

Make a map once and use it anywhere: with the “Map Studio” block, the “Map Studio” map widget in Elementor (also with the free Elementor), or with [devenzi_map id="…"] in Divi, widgets and classic themes. Change it once, and it changes everywhere.

Switching is easy

Coming from WP Go Maps, WP Maps or WP Store Locator? Map Studio finds your maps and brings them over with one click. Your pages need no changes: once you deactivate the old plugin, its shortcodes and blocks show the maps brought over. Honest comparisons: WP Go Maps, WP Maps and WP Store Locator.

Map Studio Pro

For maps that tell a story. Pro adds:

  • Story maps: while visitors scroll, the map flies from place to place and routes draw themselves.
  • Ride along and presentations: the camera flies along a route, with stops that show text, a photo and a view of their own.
  • GPX with elevation profile for hikes, bike rides and runs.
  • “How do I get there?”: visitors plan their way to a place right on your map.
  • Relief with shaded hills and real 3D mountains when you tilt the map.
  • Satellite and hybrid styles, and the Street View figure: visitors drag it onto a street and look around there.
  • Photos for new places: up to four free photos from Wikimedia Commons and Mapillary, copied into your media library with their credit.
  • Your own map data: the map of your region on your own server, so nothing is loaded from other servers.

Everything in the free version stays free and complete.

Languages

English. Translations, German among them, come through translate.wordpress.org.

External services

Map Studio relies on the third-party services below. Each one is listed with what it is used for, what is sent and when, and its terms and privacy policy. None of them needs an account unless noted. Nothing else is sent anywhere, and the plugin has no tracking.

OpenFreeMap: the map

  • What it is for: the map itself (map tiles, fonts and icons). Needed on every page with a map and in the editor.
  • What is sent and when: the visitor’s IP address and which part of the map is shown, by the visitor’s browser, when a map comes into view. With “Load maps only after a click” (Map Studio → Privacy), only after the visitor clicked “Load map”.
  • Server: tiles.openfreemap.org
  • Provider: OpenFreeMap (Hyperknot Software Kft., Hungary), delivered through Cloudflare · https://openfreemap.org/
  • Terms of service: https://openfreemap.org/tos/ · Privacy policy: https://openfreemap.org/privacy/

Photon by komoot: address search

  • What it is for: the search for addresses and places in the editor (Map Studio), name ideas (the address) for a new place, a place’s part of town, and the postcode or town visitors can type next to “Near me” in the list of places.
  • What is sent and when: in the editor, the words searched for or a new place’s coordinates, by the editor’s browser while searching or setting a place. For “Near me”, what a visitor typed, asked by your website and kept for a week; visitors never connect to Photon. Switch it off per map with “Visitors can also type a place”. The address check sends a typed address the same way and keeps nothing.
  • Server: photon.komoot.io (paths /api and /reverse)
  • Provider: komoot GmbH, Germany · https://photon.komoot.io/
  • Terms of service: https://www.komoot.com/terms-of-service · Privacy policy: https://www.komoot.com/privacy

Route planning: one service, the one you choose

A route along real roads and paths in the editor. Your website’s server asks the service chosen under Map Studio → Settings → Route planning, only while you plan a route; the route is saved with the map, and visitors never connect to the service. Sent: the route’s stops and the way of travelling, with your key if needed and your website’s address as user agent, never anything about visitors.

OpenStreetMap routing of FOSSGIS (the default, no key)
* What it is for: routes and travel-time areas in the editor, at most one request a second; never for visitors.
* Server: routing.openstreetmap.de (path /routed-foot, /routed-bike or /routed-car), valhalla1.openstreetmap.de (path /isochrone)
* Provider: FOSSGIS e.V., Germany · https://routing.openstreetmap.de/
* Terms of service: https://www.fossgis.de/arbeitsgruppen/osm-server/nutzungsbedingungen/ · Privacy policy: https://routing.openstreetmap.de/about.html (section “Privacy”)

openrouteservice (needs your own free key)
* What it is for: routes in the editor.
* Server: api.openrouteservice.org (path /v2/directions; with Pro also /geocode/autocomplete, the address search of “How do I get there?”)
* Provider: HeiGIT gGmbH, Heidelberg, Germany · https://openrouteservice.org/
* Terms of service: https://account.heigit.org/info/tos · Privacy policy: https://heigit.org/privacy-policy

GraphHopper (needs your own key)
* What it is for: routes in the editor.
* Server: graphhopper.com (path /api/1/route; with Pro also /api/1/geocode, the address search of “How do I get there?”)
* Provider: GraphHopper GmbH, Munich, Germany · https://www.graphhopper.com/
* Terms of service: https://www.graphhopper.com/terms/ · Privacy policy: https://www.graphhopper.com/privacy/

Your own OSRM or Valhalla server: only the address you enter; nothing goes to a third party.

OpenStreetMap details: Nominatim, Overpass, Wikimedia

  • What it is for: the photo, opening hours, phone, website and lines of a place (“Getting there”, and the popups of the map’s stations, shops and cafés), and the photos of the example map.
  • What is sent and when: only the place’s OpenStreetMap id, asked by your website and kept for a week. When you open the example map, your website fetches its seven photos from Wikimedia Commons once. Visitors never connect to these services; photos are copied to your website.
  • Servers: nominatim.openstreetmap.org, overpass-api.de, overpass.private.coffee (or your own Overpass server), commons.wikimedia.org, www.wikidata.org, upload.wikimedia.org, thumb.wikimedia.org
  • Terms and privacy: https://operations.osmfoundation.org/policies/nominatim/ · https://osmfoundation.org/wiki/Privacy_Policy · https://wiki.openstreetmap.org/wiki/Overpass_API · https://foundation.wikimedia.org/wiki/Policy:Terms_of_Use · https://foundation.wikimedia.org/wiki/Policy:Privacy_policy

Mapillary and Google Street View: only with your key

  • What it is for: a 360° photo at the top of a popup and a Street View button. Mapillary works with Map Studio’s shared token, which all its websites use together and Mapillary may limit; you can enter your own token or a Google key (Map Studio → Privacy).
  • What is sent and when: in the editor, the editor’s browser asks Mapillary for photos around a place. With a token of your own, the settings page tries it from your browser to show whether it works. On the site, the visitor’s browser loads the photo (with the IP address) only when a visitor opens such a popup or presses Street View.
  • Servers: graph.mapillary.com, tiles.mapillary.com, fbcdn.net; www.google.com (/maps/embed)
  • Terms and privacy: https://www.mapillary.com/terms · https://www.mapillary.com/privacy · https://cloud.google.com/maps-platform/terms · https://policies.google.com/privacy

“Get directions”: a link, if you switch it on

  • What it is for: a button in a place’s popup that opens the way there in Google Maps, Apple Maps or OpenStreetMap (as you choose).
  • What is sent and when: nothing until a visitor clicks it; then the visitor’s browser opens that site with the coordinates of the place.
  • Google: terms https://policies.google.com/terms · privacy https://policies.google.com/privacy; Apple: terms https://www.apple.com/legal/internet-services/maps/terms-en.html · privacy https://www.apple.com/legal/privacy/; OpenStreetMap: terms https://osmfoundation.org/wiki/Terms_of_Use · privacy https://osmfoundation.org/wiki/Privacy_Policy

Devenzi: feedback

  • What it is for: the “Feedback” button and the optional question when you deactivate Map Studio (admins only).
  • What is sent and when: only when you press “Send”, from your server: your text, the reason you picked, your e-mail if entered, the Map Studio and WordPress versions, admin language, screen and browser. Not your site address or user name.
  • Optional usage figures: the deactivation question shows five values next to an unticked box: days installed, number of maps, number of places, whether a map was ever saved, and whether a map is on a published page. They are sent only if you tick the box and press “Send”. “Skip” sends nothing at all. The install date and the “saved” note stay on your site in one option, without address, e-mail or ID, and are removed when you delete the plugin.
  • The optional profile: what the map is for and how big your website is stay on your site. Only if you tick the box next to the question are these two answers sent, once, from your server, without your site address, user name or any ID.
  • Server: devenzi.com
  • Provider: Devenzi (the developer of this plugin) · https://devenzi.com/
  • Privacy policy: https://devenzi.com/privacy.html · Imprint: https://devenzi.com/imprint.html

Only in Map Studio Pro

Map Studio Pro is not part of this plugin: it is a separate download from https://devenzi.com/map-studio.html, sold and delivered there by our reseller Freemius. This plugin does not connect to Freemius; its “Get Pro” and “Try Pro for free” buttons are plain links. Pro’s services, for completeness:

  • Terrain Tiles on Amazon Web Services (AWS Open Data, data by Mapzen/Tilezen, https://registry.opendata.aws/terrain-tiles/): elevation for the Relief style, loaded by the visitor’s browser only on maps in that style. AWS terms: https://aws.amazon.com/service-terms/ · Privacy: https://aws.amazon.com/privacy/
  • The Street View figure uses Google or Mapillary as above, while a visitor carries it.
  • “How do I get there?”: your website asks the route service you chose (not FOSSGIS) and its address search, or Photon with your own server, with the visitor’s start – never with the visitor’s IP address.
  • Photos for new places from Wikimedia Commons and Mapillary (see above), copied into your media library.

Map data © OpenStreetMap contributors (https://www.openstreetmap.org/copyright).

The pictures on the Map Studio start page (assets/img/hero) are maps made with the plugin: map data © OpenStreetMap contributors, OpenMapTiles, OpenFreeMap; elevation for the Alps from the Terrain Tiles (Mapzen); the aerial picture of Cologne: Land NRW (2026), Datenlizenz Deutschland – Zero – Version 2.0 (https://www.govdata.de/dl-de/zero-2-0).

Source code

The plugin bundles MapLibre GL JS 6.14.0 (BSD-3-Clause) in assets/vendor/maplibre, with its license file. Its source is at https://github.com/maplibre/maplibre-gl-js. For 360° photos it bundles MapillaryJS 4.1.2 (MIT) in assets/vendor/mapillary, with its license file; source: https://github.com/mapillary/mapillary-js. For the “Modern” style it bundles the font Inter (SIL Open Font License 1.1, https://github.com/rsms/inter) in assets/fonts, with its license file. The plugin’s own JavaScript and CSS are not minified and need no build step.
sections.installation:
1. Install Map Studio under Plugins → Add New and activate it.
  2. Go to Map Studio → New map. The full-screen editor opens.
  3. Pick a style, search or click to add places, save.
  4. In a post or page, add the “Map Studio” block and choose your map, or paste its shortcode into a page builder or widget.
sections.faq:
Do I need an API key or an account?

No. The map tiles come from OpenFreeMap, a free and open map service, and routes along real roads are planned with the free OpenStreetMap routers of FOSSGIS. There is nothing to sign up for. Optionally, you can choose openrouteservice or GraphHopper with your own key, or your own OSRM or Valhalla server, under Map Studio → Settings.

Is it really free? Are there limits?

The plugin is free. OpenFreeMap has no usage limits for normal websites. If you want to be completely independent, Map Studio Pro hosts the map data for your region on your own server and adds GPX routes with an elevation profile and story maps.

Can I try it before I install it?

Yes. “Live Preview” on this page opens Map Studio in a test WordPress right in your browser, with two demo maps: a store finder and a festival site plan. Nothing is installed on your site, and nothing you try there is kept.

Can I use it as a store locator without Google Maps?

Yes. Use the “Store finder” template or switch on the list of places. Import your locations from Excel or CSV, or bring them over from WP Store Locator, WP Go Maps or WP Maps. Visitors can search, filter by category and sort by distance from their location or a postcode, with the nearest locations first, and limit the list to a radius of 5 to 100 km.

Is it GDPR-friendly (DSGVO)?

When a map is shown, the visitor’s browser loads the map tiles from OpenFreeMap (IP address is transmitted). If you have no consent tool, switch on “Load maps only after a click” under Map Studio → Privacy: then nothing is loaded until the visitor agrees. The privacy page also gives you a text for your privacy policy. This is not legal advice. More in our guide Google Maps and the GDPR in WordPress.

Do visitors have to agree on every map? Does it work with my cookie tool?

Once a visitor clicks “Load map”, their browser remembers it (local storage, no cookie) and the other maps on your site load directly. With Pro, a map with relief or aerial images asks once more, for those servers. Map Studio also asks these cookie tools through their documented JavaScript interfaces:

  • Complianz: consent to the category “marketing”.
  • Borlabs Cookie 3: consent to a service with the ID map-studio (create it, e.g. with OpenFreeMap as provider).
  • Real Cookie Banner: consent to a service with the unique name map-studio.

Other categories or service names: the filter devenzi_map_consent_tools (keys complianz, borlabs, rcb; empty switches one off). Any other tool: call window.devenziMapConsent() in its opt-in code on every page view (or set window.devenziMapConsentGiven = true before the map script runs). To let visitors take it back as easily as they gave it, put the shortcode [devenzi_map_consent] on your privacy page: it shows a button “Withdraw my consent for maps” (the suggested privacy text already contains it). In your own code, window.devenziMapConsent( false ) does the same. When a visitor agrees with the button, the page fires the event devenzi-map-consent on document.

Can I use it with Elementor, Divi or classic themes?

Yes. In Elementor, add the “Map Studio” widget and choose your map. It shows live in the editor, with a button to the Map Studio. Everywhere else, paste the shortcode [devenzi_map id="…"] where shortcodes work (Divi, widgets, classic themes). You can also change the height: [devenzi_map id="12" height="400"].

Can I show many locations, like a store locator?

Yes. Import your locations from a table or add them one by one, then switch on the list of places. Visitors can filter by category, search, sort by distance with “Near me” (from their location or a postcode they type), and see who is open right now. The “Store finder” template sets all of this up. See also Store locator for WordPress.

Does it replace Google Maps?

For showing your locations, areas and routes: yes. “Get directions” still hands over to Google Maps, Apple Maps or OpenStreetMap, but only when a visitor clicks it. Our guide Google Maps alternative for your website compares the options.

Is it an alternative to Mapbox?

For vector maps, yes. Map Studio uses MapLibre GL JS, the open-source library that grew out of Mapbox GL JS, with tiles from OpenFreeMap. You need no account and no access token.

Can I switch from WP Go Maps, WP Maps or WP Store Locator?

Yes, and your pages need no changes. When Map Studio finds maps from WP Go Maps or WP Maps, Map Studio → Maps shows them with their markers, categories, areas, lines and circles; tick the ones you want and bring them over. The stores of WP Store Locator become one store finder map with address, phone, opening hours and categories, the list beside the map and “Near me”. Then deactivate the old plugin: its shortcodes and blocks on your pages now show the maps brought over. Activate it again and everything is as before. Google styles, your own pin images, heatmaps, image overlays and routes from Google’s directions do not come over; Map Studio lists what stays behind for each map. Step by step and side by side: WP Go Maps, WP Maps and WP Store Locator.

The map stays grey with WP Rocket, LiteSpeed Cache or another speed plugin

Options like “Delay JavaScript execution” (WP Rocket), “Load JS Delayed” (LiteSpeed Cache) or “Delay JavaScript” (Perfmatters) start scripts only after the visitor’s first click or scroll, so the map waits until then. Add these two words to the plugin’s list of exclusions: devenzi-map (the map’s scripts) and devenziMapData (its settings on the page). Nothing is lost by it: the map library itself is still loaded only when a map comes into view. Combining or minifying JavaScript is fine.

The map says “The map could not load.”

The visitor’s browser could not reach the map. Most often a blocker or a strict firewall keeps it from tiles.openfreemap.org, or the site sends a Content Security Policy without it. In that case, allow https://tiles.openfreemap.org there. “Try again” asks once more. With Map Studio Pro and your own map data, nothing has to come from other servers.

What happens when I delete the plugin?

By default, your saved maps and settings stay, so you can switch to Pro or reinstall without losing anything. To remove everything when you delete the plugin, switch on “Remove all maps and settings” under Map Studio → Settings first. Maps placed directly in posts always stay in the post content but are no longer shown without the plugin. Photos you added to a place stay in your media library either way.
sections.changelog:
1.0.1

  • New: an example map. Next to the templates, “Example map” opens a finished festival site plan with areas, routes, pins and photos as a copy of your own – to look at first, then to play with. The Live Preview on WordPress.org opens the same map.
  • New: the popups of the base map’s places (shops, stations, cafés) have a “Search the web” button, and say “No further details about this place” where the loading bars used to vanish without a word.
  • Fixed: an open popup flashed up to four times while the studio looked up the stops, address and photos of its place, and jumped between above and below its pin while the map was moved. It now stays open and keeps its side.
  • Fixed: on a tilted 3D map, a popup that is always open could be cut off at the top edge.
  • Fixed: routes with more than 2,000 points and areas with more than 500 ended in mid-way on the page. They are now simplified instead of cut off.
  • Fixed: “Put it on a page” at the end of the guide gave up without a word after 30 seconds when saving took longer (a slow host, or photos being fetched for the popup). It now waits as long as the map is being saved and says so if it still cannot finish.
  • Fixed: on tablets the settings scrolled visibly beneath their heading “Map settings”.
  • Fixed: a link straight into a map right after activating Map Studio led to the overview instead.
  • In 3D, roofs are grey in the “Colourful” and “Clear” styles too, no longer terracotta, so your places stand out.
  • With Pro: riding along a long route, the camera rises on long straights, slows down in bends and comes down to street level in good time before the destination.
  • With Pro: “Fill with booths” places at most 2,000 booths at once and says how to bring the number down (wider aisles, larger booths or a smaller area).

1.0.0

  • Booths and stalls for markets and festivals: places with a floor plan (hut, tent, stage, food truck), lined up along an axis, snapping into place, numbered, several selected and copied at once, traders from a table. With Pro: booths in 3D with roof and counter, a whole row pulled from one booth, and an area filled with booths in rows and aisles.
  • The studio on tablets and small laptops: one column at the right, or a panel at the bottom when the tablet stands, holds the steps, your places and drawings, the settings and “Next”. Much more of the map stays free.
  • On phones only the tool bar stays at the bottom: the settings open from a button in it, the list from the count in the search, “Next” sits beside the steps, and a grip closes the sheet.
  • A calmer studio: a place shows only the sections that fit its map (the rest under “More for this place”), the map settings show the most important first, there is one search, tools only at the bottom, and “Map › Place” at the top of the panel tells you where you are.
  • One colour for the studio itself: your brand colour now shows only on the map and in the previews, the active tool is dark blue.
  • Removed a place or shape by mistake? The message has an “Undo” button.
  • Help in the studio (“?”): mouse and keys, the tutorial video and questions and answers.
  • Step 2 says its settings are for this map only and links to the standard for all maps. A changed standard applies to every map that has not changed it, and the message says how many.
  • The search says when an address is only a guess, the guide asks for a name when there is only an address, and a new map starts with the whole world.
  • The map overview shows real pictures of your maps, with small pins in each place’s colour. On phones its figures stand two by two.
  • Fixed: a popup could show the details of another place at the same address (such as the café in the building); a stop served by bus and tram showed twice; the guide from “+ New map” did not save the map at “Your map is ready”; a second map of the same address got the same name; the block editor showed a shorter popup than the page; a long popup could reach under the bars of the studio; the map name was cut off on phones and tablets.

0.6.0

  • The guide saves your map at “Your map is ready” and takes you straight to a new page with the map on it, in the same tab. The shortcode for Elementor, Divi and widgets is right there to copy.
  • Fixed: on narrow or low maps, a popup that opens by itself no longer covers its pin or gets cut off, and a clicked popup leaves room for the pin.

0.5.9

  • A real store finder: search radius after “Near me”, a phone field with a call button, an “Open now” filter, address suggestions from your own places and a direct link to each place.
  • “Near me” keeps the list in place, marks the nearest store and shows the visitor and the store together on the map. With Pro, the route starts right at the visitor’s position.
  • Delivery areas from real travel times, for one place or as one calm area for all of them. Visitors can check their address against your areas; the address is not stored.
  • Import Excel files directly (.xlsx and .xlsm). They are read in your browser, nothing is uploaded.
  • The guide for a store finder asks for the name, phone and opening hours of each store, day by day.
  • The studio now leads you in three steps: design the map, see it on your page, put it on your site. New toolbar with named tools, search and undo; on phones, sheets instead of side panels.
  • Popups open either beside the map or on it, as you choose per map, and long ones scroll inside.
  • Pins can have their own border, border colour, icon colour and icon size. The selected pin glows on the ground.
  • A calmer look for all controls, with a light, slimmer toolbar.
  • A new, empty map starts with the guide, and is no longer saved until it has something in it.
  • A small, optional question about what your map is for and how big your site is adapts the recommendations. The answers stay on your site unless you tick the box to share them.
  • The boxes for API keys show their state, what the key brings, what it costs and whether you need it at all.
  • The deactivation question can include five usage figures, shown to you first, only if you tick the box.
  • The top bar, toolbar and map controls stay tidy at every window size: the steps sit above the toolbar, the map credit in the corner, zoom and compass at the edge.
  • Clicking a pin in the studio no longer changes or saves anything.
  • “Locate me” tells you when your position is missing or outside the locked map area.
  • Fixed: pins flashing when the map style changes, placeholders that kept loading in map place popups, a popup shrinking into the corner on narrow maps, a popup moving in small steps after a click in the list, and a crash with page languages such as pt-PT-ao90.

0.5.6

  • On phones, the place stays fully visible above its popup card, and when the card closes the map glides back to the place instead of leaving it at the top edge.
  • The templates “Location and directions” and “Store finder” start with the “Modern” style.
  • A place’s 360° photo no longer turns black when its popup is opened a second time. It stays loaded while the popup is closed, so it shows at once and as you turned it.
  • “Feedback” next to “New map” and in the studio: write in a few words what bothers you or what is missing – no account and no e-mail needed. Deactivating asks once, briefly and skippably, what did not fit.
  • “New map” puts “Start empty” first; the templates follow below, and none of them looks chosen before you click.
  • The Pro page keeps a readable width on very wide screens.

0.5.5

  • After activating Map Studio you land on its overview, ready to make your first map, instead of in the plugin list.
  • The controls window no longer opens by itself over the map on the first visit; a dot on its button points to it. Esc closes it, also while you type in a field.
  • A new map on a site in English (US) starts in the country of the site’s time zone, when one is chosen by city.
  • “Embed” right after a guided template saves the map and then shows its shortcode, instead of asking you to save first.
  • On phones, a place’s popup sits as a card at the bottom of the map instead of being cut off at the pin. A map too low for it grows a little.
  • A place’s name stays the name of the map, also after you add an area or a route (“Lighthouse Kitchen” no longer becomes “Map of Hamburg”).
  • Adding photos in the studio: the media window looks as it does everywhere in WordPress, without overlapping headings.
  • “Keep visitors in this area” can be switched off again: before, the saved map kept the old area. The same held for other settings taken off a map.
  • Clicking a place in the list below the map: its popup no longer jumps to the side and back. The place lands a little higher, so the popup fits below it.

0.5.4

  • Names of places, addresses and categories show on your pages exactly as typed, also with “<” or a percent sign before a letter.
  • Opening a map in the studio shows all of its places in the free area between the panels.
  • Messages in the studio no longer cover each other, so the note on rows left out of an import stays readable.
  • Bringing maps over again: the text now says that a map you changed here is kept unless you tick “Replace my changes”, and the report names the map.
  • The studio can no longer be shown inside another website.
  • The overview lines up its templates with the numbers below them, also on wide screens.
  • Routes: “Swap start and finish” turns a route around; along streets it is planned again for the other direction.
  • Drawing a route point by point, the next piece can follow the streets on foot, by bike or by car.
  • Planning a route shows it as soon as start and destination are set. Other ways are shown in grey to pick from, and “Use this route” takes the one you chose.
  • Long routes along streets show fewer points to drag; zoom in and all of them appear.
  • Edge lengths of areas and routes sit quietly outside the edge, like a measure on a plan.
  • Without 3D, buildings stay visible when zooming in closely, and “In your colour” shows them more clearly.
  • With 3D, routes and area outlines stay whole from afar and pass behind buildings close up. Buildings no longer lose walls.
  • A route across an area opens only its own popup.
  • Edge, fill, line width and line style of areas and routes are always shown now, no longer folded away under “More options”.
  • While editing an area, its size sits large and light in the middle instead of in a dark tag.
  • The studio works in two steps: “Map” for the map itself (look, your colour and pins, buildings, symbols, story map) and “On your page”, the preview inside a sketched web page, with what sits around the map (format, heading, list), what visitors can do and privacy. Each area has a head that says what it is for; the rail names them on hover.
  • Arrows and free text on the map: an arrow is drawn point by point and gets a head at its end (any route can get one); a text goes where you click, in any size, colour and turn, and keeps its angle to the streets.
  • Areas can be circles and rectangles too: a circle from its middle and edge stays round (drag its edge or type the radius), a rectangle keeps its right angles and can be turned. “Make it a free shape” turns either into an ordinary area.
  • “New map” asks first: a template that leads you through it, or an empty map. Every template now guides you step by step – place or stores (also from a table), delivery area (drawn or as a circle), route (planned along paths or drawn), areas and spots of an event, look, and what visitors get. Drawing happens right on the map, and after each step the guide says what it got.
  • Templates are only offered on a map nothing was chosen for yet, so a click on one can no longer replace your settings.
  • Map styles come in groups – standard maps, special maps, terrain and aerial – and the settings page says what sets each apart and what it suits. “Map colour” is now called “Accent colour”; a chosen colour shows its ring at once.
  • “Getting there”, the OpenStreetMap details of places (photo, lines, opening hours), the 360° photo at the top of the popup and the Street View button are now part of the free version.
  • “Pictures at the top” brings a place’s photos and its 360° view together: a slideshow of photos or a look around, one click apart. The 360° photo found stays when you switch to photos, also after saving.
  • Typing in a place’s name, address or text no longer rebuilds its open popup, so it no longer flickers; photos and the 360° view stay still.
  • Suggested categories show under the field right away, without clicking into it first.
  • A place without an address gets the one at its pin by itself.
  • The link of a place’s button takes what you type: example.com and www.… get https://, an e-mail address writes a mail, a phone number calls. Anything that is no address says so under the field and is not saved as a broken button.
  • A popup that opens half under the studio’s panels or toolbar moves into view, also when it grows while you edit it.
  • A pin’s name moves above the pin while its popup opens below, so the popup no longer covers it.
  • Dragging the map no longer stutters back and forth while details of an open popup arrive: the map is only moved for a popup you just opened or that grew, and never while it is moving.
  • 3D buildings get roofs of their own colour (terracotta on the colourful styles, a darker tone of the walls elsewhere). Buildings OpenStreetMap knows no height of no longer stand 5 m low: their height is estimated from their footprint (a garage stays low) and the buildings around them (a back house in an old-town block is as tall as its neighbours). Known heights are never changed.
  • Choosing a Street View photo or looking again for a 360° photo no longer makes the settings jump; “Look again” says what it found.
  • Pro: painting buildings on a flat map shows the outlines of all buildings.
  • Pro: deleting Pro while the free version is active no longer stops with an error.

0.5.3

This release is about not losing work.
* Two windows on the same map no longer overwrite each other. When the map was saved elsewhere in the meantime, the studio asks whether to load the newer version or keep yours.
* A map deleted in another window is not brought back by the studio’s autosave; the studio asks.
* “Recently deleted” below your maps: deleted maps can be restored from there until WordPress empties the trash. Undo after deleting now restores the map with its address.
* Import: tables with more than 500 places say so before importing, and the message afterwards names why rows were left out. Leaving the page while addresses are still being looked up asks first.
* Import: GeoJSON with multi parts comes in completely, round trips stay closed, long routes keep their last point, KML with spaces in coordinates reads correctly, and KMZ, UTF-16 tables and quote marks inside cells are handled.
* Bringing maps over from WP Go Maps, WP Maps or WP Store Locator again no longer replaces the changes you made here unless you tick “Replace my changes”. Two runs at once and maps without a usable position are handled and named in the report.
* Authors and multisite users: “&”, “<” and quotes in names stay as typed.
* “Duplicate” also works for published maps of colleagues; “Ask before deleting” can be switched off again.
* Saved maps are read over the REST API only by people who can make maps.
* Deleting the plugin with “Remove all maps and settings” switched on now also removes your personal studio preferences and the notes of imports.
* Pro: GPX files bring every track part, route and waypoint; elevation profiles no longer start at 0 m.
* Pro: photos the studio copied into the media library are only cleaned up when nothing on the site uses them any more – also not in page builders, shop galleries or custom fields – and only after a day.
* Pro: deleting a region while it downloads works reliably, and maps fall back to OpenFreeMap when a region’s file is missing.
* Pro: place details and visitor directions are shared fairly – one visitor can no longer use up the day’s limit for everyone.

0.5.2

  • A new map style, “Modern”: white streets, slate grey main roads, fresh green and clear water, with the font Inter. New sites start with it; sites that already have maps keep their default.
  • Times of day in the Modern style have colours of their own instead of a filter over the map, so names and roads stay sharp at night.
  • Routes run behind 3D buildings; the part a building hides is dotted.
  • Pick your way: after planning a route between two stops, the studio shows the other ways in grey with their length and time. Click one to take it. With openrouteservice, GraphHopper or Valhalla there is also a way without motorways.
  • Directions: a planned route keeps its turn by turn directions. Visitors open them in the route’s popup and click a step to see it on the map. You can switch them off per route.
  • Pro: the big turns of the directions become notes of the presentation with one click, and the ride shows the current step.
  • Pro: stations also list the buses and trams that stop right next to them, one row per kind.
  • Pro: your own places show the photo, lines and opening hours of the OpenStreetMap place they stand on.
  • Pro: photos from Wikimedia Commons show again in the popups of the map’s places.

0.5.1

  • Maps load faster: names that the map styles set in italic (water, places of interest) now use the regular font, so a page with a map downloads one font file less, about 45 KB.

0.5.0

  • “Near me” with a typed place: next to the button, visitors can type a postcode or town and the list is sorted by distance from there. Handy on computers without GPS. Your website looks it up, so the visitor’s IP address stays with you.
  • Buttons of places can be marked as an affiliate or sponsored link (rel=”sponsored”).
  • “Put on a new page”: one click in the studio or the overview creates a draft page with the map and opens it.
  • A heading and a short text for the map, inside its frame, so they look like part of it on any page, also with the shortcode, Elementor or Divi.
  • Places have an address: taken from the search or looked up at the pin, shown in the popup and the list. Imports from tables, WP Go Maps, WP Maps and WP Store Locator fill it.
  • New maps name themselves after their place or town (“Map of Cologne”) until you give them your own name.
  • New maps open around your last map, or in the country of your site, instead of over all of Europe. Returning users find the templates at the top of the overview.

0.4.0

  • Bring your maps over from WP Go Maps, WP Maps and WP Store Locator: Map Studio → Maps lists them with what is on them; tick and bring them over with places, categories, areas, lines and circles. The stores of WP Store Locator become one store finder with address, phone, e-mail and opening hours.
  • Your pages keep working: once the old plugin is deactivated, its shortcodes and blocks show the maps brought over. Activate it again to switch back.
  • New maps start with the “Colourful” style. Sites that already have maps keep “Light” as their default.

0.3.1

  • Popups on narrow maps and phones are no longer cut off at the edge of the map.
  • The search field of the list keeps its own size instead of taking the theme’s text size.
  • KML import: every line and area of a multi-part placemark (Google Earth, track exports) comes along, not only the first.
  • The editor in narrow windows: the top bar no longer runs under the right panel.
  • A shape left while it was still being drawn no longer stays behind empty.

0.3.0

  • The Relief style (shaded hills, 3D mountains) is now part of Map Studio Pro; this plugin loads no elevation data.
  • Draw a route by hand along the ways (straight, on foot, by bike or by car) and change its kind later.
  • Quick buttons in the list of places and shapes; a click flies there and opens the popup.
  • New places show at once; the editor stays smooth with many places.
  • Translations come from translate.wordpress.org.

0.2.0

  • Plan routes along real roads and paths with openrouteservice (your own free key), with stops you can drag and insert.
  • Stations, shops and cafés of the base map show a popup and can be added as a place, with a fitting icon and their kind as category.
  • Popups with the place’s icon and small icon buttons; per place: open on click, on hover or always; width dragged at the edge.
  • Per place: its own pin shape and size (also any size), “never group”; 66 icons with groups and search; your own colours are kept.
  • Several places at once (Shift + drag a frame, Shift or Ctrl + click, Ctrl+A): move, colour and remove them together, or connect them with a route (straight or along streets) that follows when a place moves.
  • Symbols of the map: choose which places of the base map show, by group (food, shops, bus and train, parking, fuel, playgrounds, nature …) and finer by kind.
  • Name ideas for a new place: its address with house number, the two streets of a crossing, or a business right there. One click takes the name.
  • Pro: “Getting there” in a place’s popup shows the stops around it (underground, city train, tram, bus, ferry) with their lines and minutes on foot within 5 to 20 minutes, and its part of town.
  • Pro: one click, and the place is finished. It names itself after the business or station right there, takes its icon, and finds up to four photos (Wikimedia Commons, Mapillary) that are copied into the media library with their credit; more to pick under Photos.
  • Controls in the studio, set per person under Settings: mouse buttons (“like maps”, or “like design programs”: left selects, right moves, the wheel button turns) and every key; a legend in the studio shows them.
  • Light and sky moods, and 3D buildings far into the distance. Turning a tilted map keeps what it has loaded, the other directions load in advance, and it runs smoothly: rising ground only where the land is hilly, tilt up to 65°.
  • The editor: panels as one page with your own order of topics, resizable panels, a compass, clearer spacing, modern scrollbars.
  • Fixes: points of the base map (stations, shops) were missing when zoomed in close; the open popup stays open while you edit; grouping works while designing.

0.1.0

  • First version: a full-screen map editor with templates, import and search, seven styles with relief and brand colour, places with icons, photos, formatted text and opening hours, list of places with filter, search and “Near me”, grouped pins, areas and routes with sizes, 3D buildings, load after click, saved maps with block, Elementor widget and shortcode, defaults with live preview, privacy settings.
  • German translation (du and Sie).

short_description: GDPR-friendly OpenStreetMap maps with a full-screen editor: store locator, routes, 3D buildings. No Google or API key, optionally no cookie banner.
description:
Embedding Google Maps usually means an iframe you cannot style, no places of your own, an API key with a credit card and, on top of that, a cookie banner. Map Studio works differently. It gives you modern vector maps based on OpenStreetMap, and you design them in a full-screen editor made for maps instead of filling in forms.

Use it as a store locator for your branches, a Google Maps alternative for your contact page, a location map with your own pins and markers, or an interactive map with areas and routes.

Highlights

  • A store locator with search, categories, “Near me” and opening hours.
  • 3D buildings that rise when you tilt the map, all the way to the horizon.
  • Light and sky: day, morning, evening, night, or live with the sun as it stands right now at your place.
  • Routes along real roads and paths by car, bike or on foot, with stops you drag and no key needed.
  • Your brand colour for the whole map, pins, areas and buttons.
  • A full-screen studio: click a place on the map and change it right there.
  • No API key, no account, and if the map loads only after a click, no cookie banner either.

Store locator without Google

Start with the “Store finder” template, or add a list to any map:

  • Bring in your locations for free from Excel or CSV, or from WP Store Locator, WP Go Maps or WP Maps.
  • Visitors search your list, filter by category or open now, and call a location with one tap.
  • “Near me” sorts by distance from the visitor’s location, or from a postcode or town they type (with suggestions from your locations), and they can limit the radius from 5 to 100 km.
  • “Do we deliver to you?”: visitors check an address against the areas you drew.
  • “Get directions” in the popup, a direct link to each location, and group bubbles when you have many.
  • GDPR-friendly: nothing from Google on your page, no API key, optional “load after click”.

Designing, not filling in forms

  • The map fills the screen, and three steps lead you from the design to your website.
  • Menus instead of long settings pages: every choice is shown as it will look.
  • Search an address or business with suggestions, or click a station, shop or café on the map and add it as a place.
  • Undo and redo, keyboard shortcuts, and a preview as visitors see it on computer, tablet and phone.
  • Start empty or with a template: store finder, delivery area, hiking route, event site plan.
  • Import places and shapes from a table (CSV/Excel; addresses are found automatically), Google My Maps (KML) or GeoJSON.

Your brand colour

Six map styles: light, night, colourful, clear, fjord and “Brand colour”, which recolours the whole map, pins, areas and buttons from one colour.

Your own places

  • 66 icons or a photo, as drop, circle, square or just the icon, in any size and colour, for the whole map or per place.
  • Popups with formatted text, photos to swipe through, a button to your page and “Get directions”. They open on click, on hover or stay open, beside the map or on it.
  • Stations, shops and cafés of the map, and your places on them, show their photo, opening hours and lines from OpenStreetMap; Getting there lists the stops nearby with minutes on foot.
  • A 360° photo at the top of the popup and a Street View button (Mapillary, or Google with your own key).
  • Opening hours with “Open · until 18:00” right in the popup and the list.
  • Categories as tags; highlight important places with a bigger pin, and keep them out of group bubbles.

Areas and routes

  • Draw a delivery zone, a district or a walking route on the map, or let Map Studio draw delivery areas from real travel times.
  • Plan a route along real roads, pick one of several ways, and it keeps its turn-by-turn directions.
  • Areas show their size and can have their name in the middle; routes show their length, start and finish.

3D and more

3D buildings far into the distance, a compass to turn the map, fullscreen and “my location” buttons, a night style for visitors in dark mode, and the map can be kept to one area. The map library loads only when a map comes into view.

Privacy-friendly (GDPR)

  • Optionally the map loads only after a click (“load after click”), with your own notice text.
  • A privacy page in the admin shows what is loaded when, plus a ready-made text for your privacy policy.

Saved maps and shortcode

Make a map once and use it anywhere: with the “Map Studio” block, the “Map Studio” map widget in Elementor (also with the free Elementor), or with [devenzi_map id="…"] in Divi, widgets and classic themes. Change it once, and it changes everywhere.

Switching is easy

Coming from WP Go Maps, WP Maps or WP Store Locator? Map Studio finds your maps and brings them over with one click. Your pages need no changes: once you deactivate the old plugin, its shortcodes and blocks show the maps brought over. Honest comparisons: WP Go Maps, WP Maps and WP Store Locator.

Map Studio Pro

For maps that tell a story. Pro adds:

  • Story maps: while visitors scroll, the map flies from place to place and routes draw themselves.
  • Ride along and presentations: the camera flies along a route, with stops that show text, a photo and a view of their own.
  • GPX with elevation profile for hikes, bike rides and runs.
  • “How do I get there?”: visitors plan their way to a place right on your map.
  • Relief with shaded hills and real 3D mountains when you tilt the map.
  • Satellite and hybrid styles, and the Street View figure: visitors drag it onto a street and look around there.
  • Photos for new places: up to four free photos from Wikimedia Commons and Mapillary, copied into your media library with their credit.
  • Your own map data: the map of your region on your own server, so nothing is loaded from other servers.

Everything in the free version stays free and complete.

Languages

English. Translations, German among them, come through translate.wordpress.org.

External services

Map Studio relies on the third-party services below. Each one is listed with what it is used for, what is sent and when, and its terms and privacy policy. None of them needs an account unless noted. Nothing else is sent anywhere, and the plugin has no tracking.

OpenFreeMap: the map

  • What it is for: the map itself (map tiles, fonts and icons). Needed on every page with a map and in the editor.
  • What is sent and when: the visitor’s IP address and which part of the map is shown, by the visitor’s browser, when a map comes into view. With “Load maps only after a click” (Map Studio → Privacy), only after the visitor clicked “Load map”.
  • Server: tiles.openfreemap.org
  • Provider: OpenFreeMap (Hyperknot Software Kft., Hungary), delivered through Cloudflare · https://openfreemap.org/
  • Terms of service: https://openfreemap.org/tos/ · Privacy policy: https://openfreemap.org/privacy/

Photon by komoot: address search

  • What it is for: the search for addresses and places in the editor (Map Studio), name ideas (the address) for a new place, a place’s part of town, and the postcode or town visitors can type next to “Near me” in the list of places.
  • What is sent and when: in the editor, the words searched for or a new place’s coordinates, by the editor’s browser while searching or setting a place. For “Near me”, what a visitor typed, asked by your website and kept for a week; visitors never connect to Photon. Switch it off per map with “Visitors can also type a place”. The address check sends a typed address the same way and keeps nothing.
  • Server: photon.komoot.io (paths /api and /reverse)
  • Provider: komoot GmbH, Germany · https://photon.komoot.io/
  • Terms of service: https://www.komoot.com/terms-of-service · Privacy policy: https://www.komoot.com/privacy

Route planning: one service, the one you choose

A route along real roads and paths in the editor. Your website’s server asks the service chosen under Map Studio → Settings → Route planning, only while you plan a route; the route is saved with the map, and visitors never connect to the service. Sent: the route’s stops and the way of travelling, with your key if needed and your website’s address as user agent, never anything about visitors.

OpenStreetMap routing of FOSSGIS (the default, no key)
* What it is for: routes and travel-time areas in the editor, at most one request a second; never for visitors.
* Server: routing.openstreetmap.de (path /routed-foot, /routed-bike or /routed-car), valhalla1.openstreetmap.de (path /isochrone)
* Provider: FOSSGIS e.V., Germany · https://routing.openstreetmap.de/
* Terms of service: https://www.fossgis.de/arbeitsgruppen/osm-server/nutzungsbedingungen/ · Privacy policy: https://routing.openstreetmap.de/about.html (section “Privacy”)

openrouteservice (needs your own free key)
* What it is for: routes in the editor.
* Server: api.openrouteservice.org (path /v2/directions; with Pro also /geocode/autocomplete, the address search of “How do I get there?”)
* Provider: HeiGIT gGmbH, Heidelberg, Germany · https://openrouteservice.org/
* Terms of service: https://account.heigit.org/info/tos · Privacy policy: https://heigit.org/privacy-policy

GraphHopper (needs your own key)
* What it is for: routes in the editor.
* Server: graphhopper.com (path /api/1/route; with Pro also /api/1/geocode, the address search of “How do I get there?”)
* Provider: GraphHopper GmbH, Munich, Germany · https://www.graphhopper.com/
* Terms of service: https://www.graphhopper.com/terms/ · Privacy policy: https://www.graphhopper.com/privacy/

Your own OSRM or Valhalla server: only the address you enter; nothing goes to a third party.

OpenStreetMap details: Nominatim, Overpass, Wikimedia

  • What it is for: the photo, opening hours, phone, website and lines of a place (“Getting there”, and the popups of the map’s stations, shops and cafés), and the photos of the example map.
  • What is sent and when: only the place’s OpenStreetMap id, asked by your website and kept for a week. When you open the example map, your website fetches its seven photos from Wikimedia Commons once. Visitors never connect to these services; photos are copied to your website.
  • Servers: nominatim.openstreetmap.org, overpass-api.de, overpass.private.coffee (or your own Overpass server), commons.wikimedia.org, www.wikidata.org, upload.wikimedia.org, thumb.wikimedia.org
  • Terms and privacy: https://operations.osmfoundation.org/policies/nominatim/ · https://osmfoundation.org/wiki/Privacy_Policy · https://wiki.openstreetmap.org/wiki/Overpass_API · https://foundation.wikimedia.org/wiki/Policy:Terms_of_Use · https://foundation.wikimedia.org/wiki/Policy:Privacy_policy

Mapillary and Google Street View: only with your key

  • What it is for: a 360° photo at the top of a popup and a Street View button. Mapillary works with Map Studio’s shared token, which all its websites use together and Mapillary may limit; you can enter your own token or a Google key (Map Studio → Privacy).
  • What is sent and when: in the editor, the editor’s browser asks Mapillary for photos around a place. With a token of your own, the settings page tries it from your browser to show whether it works. On the site, the visitor’s browser loads the photo (with the IP address) only when a visitor opens such a popup or presses Street View.
  • Servers: graph.mapillary.com, tiles.mapillary.com, fbcdn.net; www.google.com (/maps/embed)
  • Terms and privacy: https://www.mapillary.com/terms · https://www.mapillary.com/privacy · https://cloud.google.com/maps-platform/terms · https://policies.google.com/privacy

“Get directions”: a link, if you switch it on

  • What it is for: a button in a place’s popup that opens the way there in Google Maps, Apple Maps or OpenStreetMap (as you choose).
  • What is sent and when: nothing until a visitor clicks it; then the visitor’s browser opens that site with the coordinates of the place.
  • Google: terms https://policies.google.com/terms · privacy https://policies.google.com/privacy; Apple: terms https://www.apple.com/legal/internet-services/maps/terms-en.html · privacy https://www.apple.com/legal/privacy/; OpenStreetMap: terms https://osmfoundation.org/wiki/Terms_of_Use · privacy https://osmfoundation.org/wiki/Privacy_Policy

Devenzi: feedback

  • What it is for: the “Feedback” button and the optional question when you deactivate Map Studio (admins only).
  • What is sent and when: only when you press “Send”, from your server: your text, the reason you picked, your e-mail if entered, the Map Studio and WordPress versions, admin language, screen and browser. Not your site address or user name.
  • Optional usage figures: the deactivation question shows five values next to an unticked box: days installed, number of maps, number of places, whether a map was ever saved, and whether a map is on a published page. They are sent only if you tick the box and press “Send”. “Skip” sends nothing at all. The install date and the “saved” note stay on your site in one option, without address, e-mail or ID, and are removed when you delete the plugin.
  • The optional profile: what the map is for and how big your website is stay on your site. Only if you tick the box next to the question are these two answers sent, once, from your server, without your site address, user name or any ID.
  • Server: devenzi.com
  • Provider: Devenzi (the developer of this plugin) · https://devenzi.com/
  • Privacy policy: https://devenzi.com/privacy.html · Imprint: https://devenzi.com/imprint.html

Only in Map Studio Pro

Map Studio Pro is not part of this plugin: it is a separate download from https://devenzi.com/map-studio.html, sold and delivered there by our reseller Freemius. This plugin does not connect to Freemius; its “Get Pro” and “Try Pro for free” buttons are plain links. Pro’s services, for completeness:

  • Terrain Tiles on Amazon Web Services (AWS Open Data, data by Mapzen/Tilezen, https://registry.opendata.aws/terrain-tiles/): elevation for the Relief style, loaded by the visitor’s browser only on maps in that style. AWS terms: https://aws.amazon.com/service-terms/ · Privacy: https://aws.amazon.com/privacy/
  • The Street View figure uses Google or Mapillary as above, while a visitor carries it.
  • “How do I get there?”: your website asks the route service you chose (not FOSSGIS) and its address search, or Photon with your own server, with the visitor’s start – never with the visitor’s IP address.
  • Photos for new places from Wikimedia Commons and Mapillary (see above), copied into your media library.

Map data © OpenStreetMap contributors (https://www.openstreetmap.org/copyright).

The pictures on the Map Studio start page (assets/img/hero) are maps made with the plugin: map data © OpenStreetMap contributors, OpenMapTiles, OpenFreeMap; elevation for the Alps from the Terrain Tiles (Mapzen); the aerial picture of Cologne: Land NRW (2026), Datenlizenz Deutschland – Zero – Version 2.0 (https://www.govdata.de/dl-de/zero-2-0).

Source code

The plugin bundles MapLibre GL JS 6.14.0 (BSD-3-Clause) in assets/vendor/maplibre, with its license file. Its source is at https://github.com/maplibre/maplibre-gl-js. For 360° photos it bundles MapillaryJS 4.1.2 (MIT) in assets/vendor/mapillary, with its license file; source: https://github.com/mapillary/mapillary-js. For the “Modern” style it bundles the font Inter (SIL Open Font License 1.1, https://github.com/rsms/inter) in assets/fonts, with its license file. The plugin’s own JavaScript and CSS are not minified and need no build step.

The studio: the map in full screen, places on the left, settings on the right, tools at the bottom.
